clue.text: This writer's work, wicked, brought about complaint

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: my
OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: slang for excellent, which is A1, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A writer grumbles that a wicked piece of work gave rise to some grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' is slang praise, so it gives A1 (first-rate); 'brought about' turns it to 1A, with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-sightedness is an eye condition, and complaint is a standard word for an ailment.

clue.text: Assail post girl having wrong letters?

indicators.note: post means after, so the assail word comes after the girl word

parts.note: miss is a young woman or girl
to pelt is to assail with missiles

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a girl working in the post room who delivers the wrong letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' suggests mail; it means the letters of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A word written with incorrect characters is wrongly spelled.

clue.text: Ordered hat online without delay

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone bought a hat on the internet and wants it straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying on the nail means paying immediately, a British idiom for promptly.

clue.text: Unemployed daughter captivated by Corsica, possibly

indicators.note: captivated by says the daughter letter is held inside

parts.note: Corsica is an example of a French île, island

explanation.surface: A jobless daughter is charmed by the Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: Corsica is French, so the island word is in French: ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idle has no work, out of a job.

clue.text: Concerned about teacher following flutter occasionally

indicators.note: following says the teacher's word comes after the flutter's word

parts.note: of can mean concerning or about, as in 'a tale of woe'
to fan is to flutter, as of wings or a hand-held fan
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: Someone worries about a teacher who has taken up betting now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flutter' suggests a small bet, but here it is the motion of a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening off and on happens intermittently, now and again.

clue.text: Adventurous chap's style of waltz endlessly supporting female

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means sitting below, so it comes after
endlessly means both end letters are dropped

parts.note: the Viennese waltz is a style of the dance

explanation.surface: A daring man dances a particular waltz holding up his female partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Ranulph Fiennes is a British explorer famed for polar expeditions.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar explorer Ranulph is the best-known British adventurer of the name.

clue.text: American soda's ordered in pub for VIP

indicators.note: in says the shuffled letters go inside the pub word

parts.note: a bar serves drinks

indicators.note: ordered here means rearranged, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An American orders a soft drink in a pub, fit for a very important person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like asking for a drink but signals a rearrangement of SODAS to SSADO.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat representing a nation abroad is a high-ranking dignitary.

clue.text: Somewhere in Middle East, we're told you must purchase

indicators.note: we're told means the words are heard, not read

parts.note: an emphatic command: do buy

explanation.surface: A shopping instruction for a trip to the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf emirate is a city on the Arabian Peninsula, famous for luxury shopping.

clue.text: Part of compass that one uses for trips?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the magnetised pointer of a compass
second meaning: a syringe used to inject drugs that cause trips

explanation.walkthrough: The compass leads the reader towards travel; 'trips' are drug-induced hallucinations.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointer in a compass and a hypodermic syringe share the same name.

clue.text: A working group disturbing man's break

indicators.note: disturbing says the pieces break into the other word

parts.note: his is the man's possessive
TU is a trade union, a group of workers

explanation.surface: A union interrupts a man's holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or gap in continuity is an interval, a break.

clue.text: Day student embraced by selected attendant

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday

indicators.note: embraced by says the student letter sits inside the word for selected

parts.note: the elite are the chosen few
L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A day pupil is welcomed into some chosen group.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite is a hanger-on or follower, one who attends on a more powerful figure.

clue.text: Book with single belief regularly cited?

definitions.text: Book with single belief regularly cited?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken, starting from the first

parts.note: the word whose alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: A volume devoted to one faith that people quote all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the description: B, I, then the odd letters B, L, E of 'belief'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripture is a book of a single faith whose verses are quoted constantly.

clue.text: Pound, for example, fifth grade put in kitty

indicators.note: put in says the grade letter goes inside the kitty word

parts.note: a pot is a pool of money, as in a card game
E is the fifth grade, after A to D

explanation.surface: A pound coin and a low grade go into a shared fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money but is Ezra Pound, the American modernist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra Pound was a celebrated American writer of verse, hence an example of a versifier.

clue.text: Stop and photograph, tracking bear

indicators.note: tracking means following behind, so the photograph word comes after

parts.note: to stand something is to bear it
a still is a single photograph, as from a film

explanation.surface: A wildlife photographer halts to take a picture while following a bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete halt in movement or progress is a standstill.

clue.text: French location that might be linked with vice (harmful drugs)

parts.words: that might be linked with vice
parts.note: vice versa is a stock phrase
ill means bad or harmful
E is ecstasy, so ES is drugs

explanation.surface: A French place associated with vice and dangerous drug-taking.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as a comment on decadence but supplies two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The palace town outside Paris is a famous place in France.

clue.text: Footwear for sale all over the shop

indicators.note: all over the shop means in disarray, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Shoes on offer are scattered untidily around a store.
explanation.definitionFit: Loafers are slip-on shoes, so the plural noun is a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Piece of cloth primarily scouring hands and face?

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the next word

parts.note: a watch has hands and a face; the question mark flags this example

explanation.surface: A cloth for scrubbing one's hands and face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands and face' reads as the body parts being scrubbed, but they are the parts of a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A swatch is a small sample of fabric.

clue.text: Root perhaps with twist disfigured tree

parts.note: a crick is a painful twist or cramp in the neck or back

indicators.note: disfigured means spoiled in shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree's root, gnarled and twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Root is an England batsman; the tree imagery makes 'Root' look botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Root is an England batsman, so he is an example of a player of the sport.

clue.text: Unharmed when in this jump-suit?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone in this state is safe and sound
second meaning: a garment made as a single item

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading needs 'in' before the answer: to arrive in one piece is to be unharmed.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-in-one outfit is a single garment, and arriving intact means safe.

clue.text: Complete run that's comparatively stifling

parts.note: to close a deal is to complete it
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Finishing a run in muggy, airless weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is humid and oppressive, so the comparative form means more oppressive.

clue.text: Macho behaviour by youth claiming new territory in Midlands

parts.note: the rut is the stag's annual display of aggression

indicators.note: claiming means taking in, so the new letter goes inside

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A young man's swagger as he stakes out land in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: Rutland is England's smallest county, in the East Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The small county in the East Midlands is a region of central England.

clue.text: More work beginning to nag daydreamer

parts.note: Utopia is the book by Sir Thomas More

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Extra work starts to irritate someone lost in reverie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' looks like 'extra' but is Thomas More, the Tudor statesman, author of an ideal-state fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist who imagines perfect societies is a visionary dreamer.

clue.text: Religious sect welcome northern brat

parts.note: URC is the United Reformed Church, a British denomination
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A church group welcomes a troublesome kid from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a mischievous, scruffy child.

clue.text: Uber's first taxi to turn up in while, one reckons

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the while word

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I walked'

indicators.note: to turn up in a down clue means read upwards, so the letters go backwards
first picks the first letter of the preceding word

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: An Uber taxi finally turns up after a while, someone reckons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' in a down clue reads the pieces bottom to top; 'one reckons' is the device, not a person's opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A counting frame of beads is a device with which one does reckoning.

clue.text: Studying firearms first in command found amid rubbish

indicators.note: found amid says the other pieces sit inside the rubbish word

parts.note: balls is British slang for nonsense
1ST, with the 1 read as I
IC is short for in charge, i.e. in command

explanation.surface: A weapons enthusiast's training begins amid piles of junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballistics is the science of projectiles and guns, the field of study for firearms experts.

clue.text: Army man collects eggs, bluish-green

indicators.note: collects means takes inside, so the eggs go within

parts.note: LT is short for lieutenant
ova is Latin for eggs

explanation.surface: A soldier gathers eggs of a greenish colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovat is a muted grey-green colour used in tweeds.

clue.text: Captain putting pressure on runner

indicators.note: on says the pressure letter is placed after the runner word

parts.note: a ski runs over snow, like a sledge runner
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A team leader leans on a sprinter to go faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete; it is the blade a sledge or skier glides on.
explanation.definitionFit: Skip is short for skipper, the leader of a team or crew.

clue.text: Oil wheels around bike event

indicators.note: around says the wheels sit around the event letters

parts.note: two round wheels look like two O letters
the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

explanation.surface: Lubricating a motorbike's wheels for a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto, also attar, is a fragrant essential oil from roses.

clue.text: On the counter section of deli, Victoria polished

indicators.note: On the counter says the hidden letters are read backwards
section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Victoria behaves politely at the delicatessen counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil manners are courteous and refined, as polished behaviour is.

clue.text: Scholarly Greek count enters Israel excitedly

indicators.note: enters says the count word goes inside the other letters
excitedly says the letters of Israel are stirred up

parts.note: to tot up is to count

explanation.surface: A nobleman with a title arrives in Israel in a state of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a nobleman but is the verb meaning add up.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Athenian philosopher was the most learned of classical Greek thinkers.

clue.text: Temperature recorded in coastal reserve

indicators.note: recorded in says the temperature letter is entered inside

parts.note: seaside describes something by the coast

explanation.surface: A thermometer reading taken at a nature reserve on the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' reads as a nature reserve but is the verb meaning keep back.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something aside for later use is to keep it back, i.e. reserve it.

clue.text: In first half hour, Arsenal's fervent fans could be so

indicators.note: in first half says only the first half of each of the next words is used

parts.note: Arsenal is a London football club; half of the eight letters of Arsenal's is kept

explanation.surface: In the first half-hour of a football match, Arsenal supporters shout themselves out.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club; 'first half' reads as part of a match but asks for the first half of 'hour' and of 'Arsenal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fans who have been shouting all match end up with rough, croaky voices.
